Priya to scope benchmark tests for Acme POC and send test plan by 2027-03-22
Schedule exec intro with Meridian SVP of Sales - target week of 2027-03-29
Joint pricing proposal for Acme account due 2027-03-24
Rosa/Liam to confirm customer stakeholders for pilot by 2027-03-18
action_items: Alex Moreno: share updated co-sell deck + pipeline spreadsheet (due 2027-03-17)
Priya Singh: define benchmark test plan and infra needs for Acme POC (due 2027-03-22)
Rosa Diaz: confirm technical contacts and data residency reqs for Acme (due 2027-03-18)
Jordan Hayes: share Meridian's Q2 co-sell targets and motion preferences (due 2027-03-19)

meeting_header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Wu (Redwood CSM); Jordan Hayes (Meridian Channel Lead), Samira Patel (Meridian Head of Sales), Liam Chen (Meridian AE), Rosa Diaz (Meridian Solutions Architect)
Agenda: pipeline review + deal strategy, co-sell motions, technical blockers, next steps
Shared: co-sell deck (link), joint pipeline spreadsheet (link)
summary: High-level pipeline review for Meridian-led co-sell opportunities. Focus on Acme pilot (largest near-term opp), alignment on roles for Q2 co-sell targets, next steps to run a benchmark and supply a pricing proposal. Technical questions around private deployment and data residency from Meridian; Redwood AE/SE to follow up with benchmark scoping and security docs.
topics: Technical requirements: VPC, data residency, SOC2/KMS
Benchmark plan for latency/cost for Acme use case
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Jordan, Samira, thanks for making time. We have about 50 minutes, we'll run through the pipeline then open for questions.
[00:18] Jordan Hayes: Yeah thanks Alex, um quick note, we've got Samira and Liam on because we want alignment for the Acme deal, that's the big one.
[00:30] Priya Singh: Cool, I'll jump into the technical asks later. Quick question on agenda, Alex, are we also covering pricing today?
[00:36] Alex Moreno: Briefly we'll capture pricing actions, we'll produce a joint proposal after we align on scope.
[00:42] Samira Patel: Sounds good.
[00:45] [01:05] Liam Chen: For Acme timeline, they're expecting a pilot in early April, like 4\u20136 week pilot, assuming procurement moves fast.
[01:15] Alex Moreno: Great. On Redwood side, our recommended path is run the pilot on Dedicated if they want predictable throughput, but we can do hosted for speed to market. There are tradeoffs latency vs cost vs isolation.
[01:32] Jordan Hayes: Right, they care about data isolation and audit logs. They asked about VPC and KMS options.
[01:38] Priya Singh: We have Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated options. For a 4\u20136 week pilot would recommend Redwood Dedicated with optional VPC peering for the pilot; Private is doable but adds lead time for network setup.
[01:54] Rosa Diaz: How long is the lead time for Private? Procurement will push back if it delays demo.
[01:58] Priya Singh: Private can be a few weeks to a month depending on KMS/HSM and legal; Dedicated is faster, like days to set up reserved capacity in a region.
[02:10] [02:40] Jordan Hayes: Ok, so for pilot we prefer Dedicated. We want to capture that in the joint proposal. Also want clarity on support SLAs and who owns first-line support.
[02:52] Ethan Wu: Redwood can do triage and we typically set up a joint support path with the partner. For enterprise deals we add a CSM and 24/7 on-call per SLA line items.
[03:04] Samira Patel: Good. On revenue splits Meridian usually does partner ops where we handle GTM and Redwood handles product delivery, we need a split that makes sense for both sides.
[03:16] Alex Moreno: Understood. We'll draft a revenue share example in the pricing proposal. Also we'll list roles in the pipeline spreadsheet so it's explicit.
[03:25] [04:05] Priya Singh: Technical note for the pilot: Acme's LLM workload is about 20k tokens/day with spiky bursts we should benchmark with our KV cache + batching settings; that will materially impact cost.
[04:18] Rosa Diaz: They also require UK data residency for some customer data do you support multi-region deployments?
[04:25] Priya Singh: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning and we can run the pilot in eu-west-2 for UK residency; if they need on-prem it's a different discussion.
[04:34] Liam Chen: Is there an SSO/SAML integration for Meridian's internal tools and for Acme?
[04:39] Alex Moreno: Yes, we support SSO via SAML/SCIM and can integrate with the customer's IdP. We'll share the security docs.
[04:45] [05:10] Jordan Hayes: Great. On the Acme commercial ask they want a fixed monthly cap for pilot so they don't get surprised. Can Redwood support caps and alerts?
[05:19] Alex Moreno: Yes, we can set quotas and spend alerts; also recommend we run a small benchmark so the cap is set with data.
[05:26] Priya Singh: For the benchmark we'll need a sample prompt set and expected traffic pattern we'll measure latency P95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens across Dedicated vs hosted.
[05:36] [06:10] Samira Patel: Perfect we'll send sample prompts and any privacy constraints.
[06:15] Priya Singh: Also quick note depending on model selection, quantized variants reduce cost but can impact quality. We'll include model/quantization tradeoffs in the test plan.
[06:28] Alex Moreno: Good call. Liam, Rosa, are you comfortable with Redwood running the benchmark for Acme as a joint engineering test?
[06:36] Liam Chen: Yes, we just need timelines.
[06:40] [07:00] Alex Moreno: Proposed timeline: pipeline spreadsheet update this week, benchmark scoping by next Monday, run benchmark the week of 3/22, proposal out 3/24, exec intro after proposal. Thoughts?
[07:12] Jordan Hayes: That maps to Meridian's Q2 motion. Let's try to hit proposal 3/24.
[07:19] [07:40] Rosa Diaz: Technical Q can Redwood's runtime be pinned to a single GPU family? We have compliance constraints that prefer NVidia A100.
[07:50] Priya Singh: We can target specific instance types for Dedicated pools, yes; we'll note that in the POC plan. There might be small perf differences but generally yes.
[07:59] [08:30] Samira Patel: Any competitors in play? Acme also talked to Databricks and Anthropic. We need concrete differentiators.
[08:40] Alex Moreno: Differentiators are production-first serving (latency/cost controls), unified runtime for private/dedicated/hosted, and observability token-level cost breakdowns and rollouts. We'll include a one-pager comparing features.
[08:56] [09:20] Priya Singh: On the technical side, call out KV cache, continuous batching, and quantization profiles those are levers to control unit economics.
[09:28] [10:00] Liam Chen: For commercial, can you share example pricing band for Dedicated for the Acme footprint?
[10:08] Alex Moreno: We'll share ranges in the proposal. For headline, Dedicated gives better predictability and lower P95 latency but higher baseline commit; hosted lower commit but higher burst costs.
[10:22] [11:00] Jordan Hayes: Ok, on enablement Meridian sales team wants a one-hour training + playbook. Can Redwood provide that?
[11:09] Ethan Wu: Yes, Redwood can run partner enablement: one-hour technial + 30min sales playbook session, and we'll hand over co-sell assets.
[11:19] Samira Patel: We'll take that.
[11:25] [12:05] Priya Singh: Quick note about security review they asked about SOC2 and audit logs. We have SOC2 and provide audit logs + exportable traces; we'll share the compliance pack.
[12:20] Rosa Diaz: And encryption at rest with KMS?
[12:24] Priya Singh: Supported. We'll include KMS notes and HSM options for Private.
[12:31] [13:00] Alex Moreno: Great. Who will own reaching out to Acme procurement? Meridian or Redwood?
[13:07] Liam Chen: Meridian will front procurement but we may loop in Redwood for contract/legal.
[13:12] Alex Moreno: Sounds good. We'll prepare a statement of work template to accelerate legal review.
[13:20] [14:00] Jordan Hayes: A couple of tricky accounts on the pipeline one is NovaHealth, they have strict PHI rules. We think Private or on-prem is required.
[14:12] Priya Singh: If PHI is involved, Private or a dedicated on-prem model is recommended. We'll follow up with detailed requirements.
[14:22] [15:00] Samira Patel: Back to Acme is there a recommended model family? Acme cares about concise answers and factuality.
[15:09] Priya Singh: For that use case we often recommend instruction-tuned smaller LLMs with classification/regeneration for factuality; we'll include model recommendations in the test plan.
[15:22] [16:00] Alex Moreno: Ok let's go through the pipeline doc Jordan, can you confirm the top three Meridian-led opps?
[16:08] Jordan Hayes: Sure: Acme (pilot target Apr), NovaHealth (PHI, longer lead), and Orion Logistics (PoC in May).
[16:20] [16:45] Liam Chen: For Orion Logistics we have an existing AWS account preference; they asked about cost per token and burst support.
[16:52] Priya Singh: We'll include burst/bucketed pricing and autoscaling policies in proposal.
[17:03] [17:30] Rosa Diaz: Any constraints on the benchmark infra we need to know? I.e., sample size, tokens, synthetic vs production traces?
[17:38] Priya Singh: Prefer production-like traces and a representative prompt set Samira said she'll share sample prompts. Also need expected concurrent requests and token distribution.
[17:52] Samira Patel: We'll provide that by Friday.
[18:00] [18:40] Alex Moreno: On the co-sell split, Jordan, can you share Meridian's typical revenue split range so we can use it as an input to the proposal?
[18:49] Jordan Hayes: Typically 70/30 or 60/40 depending on who owns the customer acquisition. For Acme I'd expect 60/40 in Meridian's favor since they lead GTM.
[18:58] Alex Moreno: Ok we'll default to a 60/40 draft and call it out as negotiable.
[19:05] [20:00] Priya Singh: Technical risk list data residency, IdP integration, rate-limit spikes. We'll assign owners in the action items.
[20:11] [21:00] Ethan Wu: I'll add the joint opp to CRM and ensure it's visible to both teams. CRM id is CRM-789345.
[21:08] [22:00] Samira Patel: Any legal questions we should flag early? Contracting timelines?
[22:12] Alex Moreno: We'll attach a draft SOW and MSA templates to speed legal review.
[22:20] [23:00] Jordan Hayes: Ok let's confirm people for the benchmark: Priya (Redwood SE) leads benchmarks, Rosa and Liam will provide environment details, Alex to coordinate commercial.
[23:12] [24:00] Priya Singh: I'll prepare a test plan doc and share it with the group.
[24:06] [25:00] Alex Moreno: Anything else on the pipeline?
[25:05] Liam Chen: Just one ask if we run into perf issues, can Redwood provide a fallback to a cheaper hosted model variant to keep demo stable?
[25:17] Priya Singh: Yes, we can configure a fallback policy to a lower-cost hosted variant during spikes.
[25:25] [26:00] Samira Patel: Great. On the enablement timing we prefer the training the week after proposal.
[26:08] Ethan Wu: Noted.
[26:14] [27:00] Jordan Hayes: Let's recap the actions Alex will share deck + pipeline, Priya will share test plan, Rosa will confirm customer contacts, Jordan will send co-sell targets.
[27:25] Alex Moreno: Yep. Any final questions?
[27:30] Rosa Diaz: One small one do you have any references of similar healthcare/regulatory pilots?
[27:36] Priya Singh: We have a case study for a regulated financial customer; we'll share but note PHI differs so we'll vet.
[27:45] [28:20] Samira Patel: Ok thanks everyone this was productive.
[28:25] Alex Moreno: Thanks all we'll aim to get the deliverables out this week.
[28:30] [29:00] Liam Chen: Thanks.
[29:05] Jordan Hayes: Bye.
